description: NAD cofactor pair: NAD (NAD⁺ oxidized) and NDH (NADH reduced; 1,4-dihydronicotinamide). Same nicotinamide chemistry as the NADP pair, minus the 2'-phosphate.
methodology: Fragment-typed force-field parameters for the NAD redox pair, oxidized NAD+ and reduced NADH (1,4-dihydronicotinamide), AMBER ff14SB/ff19SB-compatible. Both oxidation states of the nicotinamide are parameterized de novo. The oxidized aromatic nicotinamide-plus-carboxamide and the reduced 1,4-dihydronicotinamide-plus-carboxamide receive separate fragment-scoped atom-type sets, each with its own Seminario-fit bonds and angles and each shared with the corresponding NADP residue so the two nucleotides never overwrite one another's terms. The Walker NAD+ contribution enters only as transferred proper-torsion values placed on these fragment types; its atom types and bonded force constants are not used. Adenine and both riboses inherit ff14SB nucleic-acid types and the pyrophosphate inherits Meagher polyphosphate parameters. Partial charges are whole-molecule, two-stage restrained (Bayly) RESP fits to a gas-phase HF/6-31G(d) Merz-Kollman ESP at four RBRA reorientations on a B3LYP/6-31+G(d) PCM(water) geometry. Bonds and angles for both nicotinamide fragments are Seminario fits to the B3LYP/6-31+G(d)/PCM(water) QM Hessian (interior terms from capped-fragment Hessians, junction terms from the whole residue), with a few phosphate terms forked from parm10/Meagher. Proper dihedrals are full multi-term GAFF2 potentials transferred by substitution together with the Walker torsions noted above, and improper planarity terms are tLEaP-perceived AMBER terms (the sp3 C4 of the reduced ring carries none); neither dihedral class is QM-derived. Every frcmod is a delta-only file layered on parm10/gaff2.
references: Fragment-typed cofactor force-field library, v1.0 (20 redox-active residues across the FMN, FAD, NADP, NAD, and biopterin families). See the 'methodology' field for the full derivation. Non-redox-active atoms use established AMBER parameters (ff14SB nucleic acids, Walker NAD+ contrib, Meagher polyphosphate).
Walker NAD+ contrib parameters (Walker, in AmberTools dat/contrib/NADH_and_NAD+/).
ff14SB nucleic acid types from parm10 + bsc1 + OL3 dihedrals (leaprc.RNA.OL3).

default.electronic_config: NAD — Walker NAD+ types only (no fragment-typed atoms)

Guberman_NAD_RESP.description: Constrained-geometry-optimization RESP charges + Seminario bonded parameters on redox-active fragment atoms + validated AMBER libraries (ff14SB / Walker NAD+ / Meagher polyphosphate) for non-redox-active atoms. Multi-cofactor-safe by construction (cross-residue same-fragment-type bonds are bit-identical).
Guberman_NAD_RESP.reference: Fragment-typed cofactor force field library, v1.0. 20 redox-active residues across FMN, FAD, NADP, NAD, and biopterin families. Each residue's frcmod is self-contained (merged from per-fragment Seminario frcmod + cofactor-to-protein linker + residue-specific cross-source params + cross-residue patches). with validated AMBER libs (ff14SB nucleic acids, Walker NAD+ contrib, Meagher polyphosphate) for non-redox-active atoms.
Guberman_NAD_RESP.name: NAD⁺ oxidized
Guberman_NAD_RESP.methodology:
This is a 'lean' add-on parameter file (an AMBER frcmod): it holds ONLY the force-field terms that the standard base force fields (loaded first) do not already supply, so nothing is duplicated. Here the base is ff14SB/parm10 (standard protein, adenine and ribose types); leaprc.RNA.OL3 is recommended (not required) to sharpen adenine dihedral accuracy. A force field models the molecule's energy with a few simple terms; here is where each one came from, in plain terms:

- Atomic charges (the partial electric charge on each atom, which sets the electrostatic forces) come from RESP, the standard recipe that adjusts the charges until they reproduce the molecule's quantum-mechanical (QM) electrostatic field. The field is sampled (Merz-Kollman scheme) over four molecular orientations and averaged, then fit in the usual two-stage (Bayly-Cieplak) way, held to the molecule's whole-number net charge. Charges were fit separately for each oxidation/protonation state and are unchanged by the atom-type relabeling below.
- Custom atom types: the redox-active ring atoms are given short custom type names so each state's distinct chemistry stays separate from the standard regions. This relabeling is value-neutral (a custom type keeps the same charge and atom 'size' as the type its atoms had before) and the types' element + hybridization are registered up front so implicit-solvent (Born) radii come out right.
- Van der Waals (each atom's effective size and 'stickiness', i.e. its Lennard-Jones radius and well depth): inherited unchanged from the source type each custom type maps to; no new values are invented.
- Bond and angle stiffness (how hard it is to stretch a bond or bend an angle, plus their rest values): from the Seminario method, which reads these constants directly off the QM second-derivative matrix (the 'Hessian') of the optimized geometry, instead of using rule-of-thumb estimates. Terms wholly inside the redox ring use an isolated-fragment Hessian; terms at a junction (where the ring meets a standard region, or where two base force fields meet) get a fresh value from the whole-molecule Hessian so the cross-boundary coupling is captured.
- Dihedrals/torsions (the energy of twisting around a bond): the Hessian gives only bonds/angles, so torsions are taken as complete (untruncated) Fourier series from the Walker NAD+/NADH set (a published, purpose-fit nicotinamide torsion set from AmberTools), relabeled onto the custom types by atom role - one consistent treatment for both oxidation states.
- Impropers: none. The nicotinamide ring needs no separate planarity terms (the Walker parameterization keeps the ring flat through its torsions).
- Phosphate: the pyrophosphate's terminal oxygens use the O3 type (Meagher 2003; mass and van der Waals equal to standard O2, bond/angle values transferred from parm10 O2), and the bridging oxygen is a custom OD type with its own Seminario values.
- Cross-cofactor consistency: where a structural unit is SHARED with the other flavin/nicotinamide cofactors (the sugar-to-phosphate ester linkage, the pyrophosphate bridge, and the ring atoms common to both), its Seminario bond/angle values are set to the average across those cofactors, so a structure holding more than one cofactor (e.g. FAD and FMN, or FAD and NAD) uses one consistent value per shared unit; the spread being averaged is within force-field accuracy.

Geometry was a DFT optimization (one conformer per state). Every state was checked to build a complete tleap topology with no missing parameters.

References: Seminario 1996 (bonded constants from the QM Hessian); Bayly-Cieplak-Cornell-Kollman 1993 (two-stage RESP); Meagher 2003 (polyphosphate O3 oxygen type); Walker (NAD+/NADH torsions, AmberTools).

prerequisites.leaprc_groups_notes: Lean (delta-only) frcmod: builds with only a standard AMBER protein FF (ff14SB->parm10 or ff19SB->parm19, which carry the nucleic-acid base/sugar params) plus addAtomTypes for the custom fragment types (emitted from atom_types) and the bundled O3 terminal-phosphate fork. leaprc.RNA.OL3 is RECOMMENDED (not required) for improved adenine dihedral accuracy. No gaff2, no meagher (the only meagher term needed, O3 vdW = O2, is folded into the frcmod).
